summary: The code change is sound and well tested, and it fixes the class of fault. Two causes left a dispatched job with no outcome. First, a run that hit an error after the Dispatch commit returned with no closing record. Second, `interrupted_work` covered only the drained channels and hid any job that a later request named as a retry, even when that retry was dropped. Now a run that errors after dispatch closes the job `failed` with an `environment:` reason. Drain lists a dispatched job with no process on every channel, and it treats a job as having a process when the job lock is held, not only when the job is in the registry. A new settle step closes an original once its retry has ended, and at the end of the drain it writes a `held <job>: <reason>` note for every dispatched job still left without an outcome. I ran the new tests and all pass: 12 drain tests, 3 run tests, the steward tests and the mirrors test. fmt, clippy and test passed in CI. The verdict is still fail, because of criterion 4. The records snapshot is current to 2026-11-08, and in it 4 of the 6 named jobs still have no outcome.json: g63s, 77zh, w1y3 and z7sj. The changelog states, and the snapshot confirms, that each was retried and the retry landed (xncn, pnjn, qjzx, ykmf). msh3 and hvyb are closed, but their reasons do not cite a commit hash. The fix for this is an operator step on the live records, not a code change. Running one drain on the new build would also close the four automatically, but the reason would name the retry job, not the commit.
